title: Compact Hom commutes with sequential homotopy colimits
statement: Let C be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] with arbitrary coproducts, and let K be a compact object [def-pc-compact-object] of C. For a sequence X_0 \to X_1 \to \cdots and a homotopy colimit X given by the distinguished triangle \bigoplus_n X_n \xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}} \bigoplus_n X_n \to X \to (\bigoplus_n X_n)[1], the canonical map \varinjlim_n Hom_C(K,X_n) \to Hom_C(K,X) is bijective.

proof.text: Compactness identifies Hom(K, coproduct E) with the direct sum of Hom(K,E_i). Coproduct projections recover each component: prove this by DirectSum induction. Thus a map into the coproduct whose projections vanish is zero. For the telescope shift s, s followed by projection 0 is zero, and s followed by projection n+1 is projection n followed by the transition. Induction proves that f composed with 1-s equal to zero implies f equal to zero. Transport this calculation through the coproduct comparison of the shift equivalence to obtain the same zero-kernel property for (1-s)[1].

Consecutive compositions in the telescope triangle vanish. Its stage maps are successor-compatible, hence compatible with all transition maps by natural-number induction. The shifted zero-kernel property kills every composite K to Y to A[1]. Triangle.coyoneda_exact₃ now gives surjectivity of postcomposition with q. Triangle.coyoneda_exact₂ identifies a map in the kernel of postcomposition with q as a telescope boundary.

Build the comparison phi with a Type-valued cocone and colimit.desc. To prove surjectivity, use compactness and DirectSum induction to combine any finite sum of stage maps into a single stage, taking max at each addition. To prove injectivity, represent both colimit elements at stages n,m, transport them to k=max(n,m), and apply exactness to their difference. Its telescope-boundary preimage has finite support by compactness. Define p_l:A to X_l by the transition on stages j<=l and zero otherwise. Each boundary summand at j<l is killed by p_l because functoriality identifies its two terms. DirectSum induction provides a bound for the whole boundary preimage. Taking l at least that bound and k shows that the difference vanishes at stage l. Types.colimit_sound' then identifies the representatives. No quotient or abelian-colimit identification is required.

lean.statement: theorem compact_hom_hocolim {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ] [Preadditive C] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C] [IsTriangulated C] [HasCoproducts.{w} C] (K : C) (hK : IsCompactObject K) (X : ℕ ⥤ C) (Y : C) (q : (∐ fun n : ULift.{w} ℕ ↦ X.obj n.down) ⟶ Y) (r : Y ⟶ (∐ fun n : ULift.{w} ℕ ↦ X.obj n.down)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧) (hT : Triangle.mk (𝟙 (∐ fun n : ULift.{w} ℕ ↦ X.obj n.down) - Sigma.desc (fun n : ULift.{w} ℕ ↦ X.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n.down)) ≫ Sigma.ι (fun k : ULift.{w} ℕ ↦ X.obj k.down) ⟨n.down + 1⟩)) q r ∈ distTriang C) : ∃ φ : colimit (X ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op K)) → (K ⟶ Y), (∀ (n : ℕ) (f : K ⟶ X.obj n), φ (colimit.ι (X ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op K)) n f) = f ≫ Sigma.ι (fun k : ULift.{w} ℕ ↦ X.obj k.down) ⟨n⟩ ≫ q) ∧ Function.Bijective φ
